title: Result.match requires both the success and the error branch
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Matching and Transformation': 'match MUST require both success and error branches.' EVIDENCE for the stock TypeScript code: the runtime's Result.match signature takes `{ readonly ok: (value: A) => Ok; readonly error: (error: E) => Failure }` (poc/src/runtime/result.ts), so an object literal carrying only `ok` is not assignable and the emitted TypeScript is rejected by the stock checker with TS2345 at the argument. specification/compatibility.mdx §3 makes that the right mechanism: the requirement is expressed in ordinary TypeScript types, so ordinary TypeScript checking enforces it. The diagnostic is reached through the emit-check stage, which is why this case also exercises the second half of the frontend's two-stage acceptance.
